approved: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Exploitation of Indigenous Culture) Bill 2017
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would change the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 to stop non-Indigenous Australians and foreigners from making money off Indigenous art, souvenirs, and other cultural expressions.
It would set up a new committee, funded from normal budget supply, to oversee these changes.
The bill would start the day after it receives Royal Assent.
The bill would amend the Competition and Consumer Act 2010.
The bill would establish a new committee.
The bill would commence the day after Royal Assent.
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, Indigenous artists, and those who sell Indigenous-style art and souvenirs.
